summary: As of October 8, 2026, junk-bond spreads are 3.15 percentage points and are down 0.09 percentage points over five trading days. Investment-grade spreads are down 0.04 percentage points over those same five trading days. The CCC-minus-BB gap is 10.58 percentage points. Of the 0.11 percentage-point move in the all-in junk yield, 0.09 was the credit spread and 0.02 was Treasury rates. The 10-year yield is 5.22 percent as of October 8, 2026 and the 30-year is 5.60 percent as of October 8, 2026, a gap of 0.38 percentage points. Brent is 104.43 dollars a barrel as of October 9, 2026 (+2.13 percent over five trading days), and the curve is backwardation. The 5-year inflation breakeven is 2.34 percent as of October 9, 2026, down 0.03 percentage points over five observations. The 10-year real yield is 2.87 percent as of October 8, 2026. The broad dollar index is 121.38 as of October 2, 2026, +3.25 index points over 20 observations. VIX is 15.41 as of October 8, 2026. The Fed balance sheet is 6.75 trillion dollars as of October 7, 2026, up 7 billion dollars over the latest four weekly observations. Reserve balances are 3.03 trillion dollars as of October 7, 2026, up 38 billion dollars over the latest four weekly observations. Overnight reverse repo is 0.3 billion dollars as of October 9, 2026, down 0.704 billion over the latest four observations.
